newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ planemaker sets sights on big Thai contract.
newsitem.headline: NZ planemaker sets sights on big Thai contract.

text.p: Hamilton planemaker Pacific Aerospace Corporation could be about to win its biggest contract ever, building 24 trainer aircraft worth NZ$17.5 million for the Royal Thai Airforce, the New Zealand Press Association reported on Monday.
If the company is successful it would mean secure jobs for 23 additional staff and another injection of wages into the Hamilton economy.
General manager Graeme Polley said PAC would get an answer from Thailand by mid-October, but had been told its chances were very good.

Meanwhile, he said PAC, bought last year in a rundown state by Hamilton's Aeromotive Corporation, was making strides with bright prospects for South American plane building contracts. Five $1 million Cresco aircraft were ordered and paid for, and a training school to produce semi-skilled aircraft builders was about to kick off.
PAC's staff had risen from 51 to 79 in the past 3-1/2 months, Polley said, adding that the Thailand government contract would mean a steady employment roll of about 100.
